title: How do orange and apple juice mix in a fruit drink?
description: The amounts of orange juice and apple juice are written as a ratio and reduced by the highest common factor until the two terms share no factor except one.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide by the highest common factor so the ratio cannot be reduced any more. Watch for students who stop after dividing by a smaller common factor.

video_script.why: The child reduces a ratio with large terms to the simplest form using the highest common factor.
video_script.substitution: Write orange juice to apple juice, divide both terms by their highest common factor, then check by multiplying back.
video_script.anchor: two jugs, Ziva's 600 mL of orange juice and 900 mL of apple juice
video_script.payoff_line: Orange juice to apple juice is two to three.

names.Ziva: mixes orange juice and apple juice to make a fruit drink

maths_rules: orange juice to apple juice is 600 : 900
600 ÷ 300 = 2 and 900 ÷ 300 = 3, so the simplest form is 2 : 3
check: 2 × 300 = 600 and 3 × 300 = 900; 2 and 3 share no factor except 1
video_script.design: One idea: divide by the highest common factor to reach the simplest form. Uses the simplest form step of the solved example. The two jugs stay for the whole video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; two jugs of Ziva: orange juice 600 mL and apple juice 900 mL

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.jugs: two jugs appear, one of orange juice marked 600 mL and one of apple juice marked 900 mL
marks.ask: the words orange : apple = ? appear between the jugs

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a fruit drink.
<bookmark mark='jugs'/>Ziva mixes six hundred millilitres of orange juice with nine hundred millilitres of apple juice.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the ratio of orange juice to apple juice in the smallest whole numbers?

beats.on_screen: the two jugs hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a ratio with an arrow ÷ highest common factor on each term, giving the simplest form

marks.same: a ratio appears with two empty boxes beside it
marks.hcf: an arrow marked ÷ highest common factor lands on each term
marks.simple: the reduced ratio is written with the words simplest form

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='hcf'/>The highest common factor is the largest number that divides both terms.
<bookmark mark='simple'/>Dividing both terms by it gives a ratio called its simplest form.

beats.on_screen: Given: orange juice 600 mL, apple juice 900 mL

marks.given: the two amounts are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, orange juice is six hundred millilitres and apple juice is nine hundred millilitres.

beats.on_screen: To find: orange juice : apple juice in simplest form

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the ratio of orange juice to apple juice in simplest form.
<bookmark mark='o'/>Step one, write the orange juice first, which is six hundred.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Then write the apple juice, which is nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='r'/>The ratio is six hundred to nine hundred.

marks.hcf: HCF is 300 is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step two, six hundred is two times three hundred.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Nine hundred is three times three hundred.
<bookmark mark='hcf'/>The highest common factor is three hundred.

beats.on_screen: 600 ÷ 300 = 2 and 900 ÷ 300 = 3, so the simplest form is 2 : 3

marks.s: 2 : 3 is boxed as the simplest form

narration: <bookmark mark='w'/>Step three, divide both terms by three hundred.
Six hundred divided by three hundred is two.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Nine hundred divided by three hundred is three.
<bookmark mark='s'/>The simplest form is two to three.

beats.on_screen: Check: 2 × 300 = 600 and 3 × 300 = 900; 2 and 3 share no factor except 1

marks.chk: the words Check: multiply back are written
marks.only: 2 and 3 are circled with the words only 1 in common

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check by multiplying back by three hundred.
<bookmark mark='mul'/>Two times three hundred is six hundred, and three times three hundred is nine hundred.
<bookmark mark='only'/>Two and three share no factor except one, so we cannot reduce any more.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Orange juice to apple juice is two to three.
